correctness.rationale: The centered stable Lévy measure has density c|h|^{-1-α}; a one-large-jump compensated Lévy–Itô estimate gives the complete first-order time/pre-location/overshoot measure. The exact renewal transform is numerator [marked successful excursion] divided by 1 minus [failed excursion transform]. Its expansion yields Exp(a) lifetime and independent Exp(r) successful age and exterior jump mark. The stopped Poisson martingale and E S~L^α/a prove reset-count coupling. Exterior integration confirms a± and centered Pareto tail. The proof assumes fixed interior λ and fixed r; simulations corroborate but are not substitutes.

originality.rationale: The object is a five-coordinate marked weak law coupling a macroscopic escape time and reset count to microscopic final-excursion age, pre-exit location, and full exterior overshoot. The 2026 primary paper explicitly derives leading mean exit time, the 2023 general reset theorem gives the exponential time marginal, the 2024 target-selection paper gives the side marginals, and earlier heavy-tail metastability gives joint time/location for smooth attracting dynamics without hard Poisson resetting. None of the inspected statements supplies the specific full joint mark law or its conditional factorization. This is a qualified best-knowledge originality assessment, not proof of priority.

value.rationale: The 2026 first-moment asymptotic leaves open spatial escape marks and the last-reset timing, which are natural observables in heavy-tailed transport and first-exit experiments. The theorem gives a single explicit joint law with nontrivial dependence (reset count locked to lifetime) and independent terminal age, jump overshoot, and macroscopic lifetime; it separates two time scales and computes an entire observable distribution rather than a marginal mean or routine substitution.
